result: Exact rmcp-v3.1.4 TaskManager cancellation tests pin the acknowledgement boundary more tightly: a tasks/get immediately after cancel_task returns is explicitly allowed and tested to remain nonterminal; cancellation does not force Task status to cancelled. The operation later determines the terminal result: TaskExit::Cancelled settles cancelled, TaskExit::Error settles failed, and successful work despite cancellation settles completed. For a persistent application, the minimum inferred contract is to authorize first, durably record cancellation intent for the stable task identity before ack, make every restart/redrive/claim consult that record, and fence superseded attempt/status writes with a monotonic generation or equivalent CAS. This still cannot prove an already-entered external effect stopped, so non-idempotent effects retain a separate idempotency/fencing obligation.
